prompt: A set of $8$ numbers has a mean of $15$. If the number $22$ is removed from the set, what is the mean of the remaining numbers?
hint: A mean alone does not tell you the individual numbers, but it does tell you their total. Start from that total.

hints.text: A mean alone does not tell you the individual numbers, but it does tell you their total. Start from that total.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try a tiny set: three numbers with mean $10$ total $30$. Remove a $12$ and $18$ is left across two numbers, so the new mean is $9$. Always convert the mean to a total first.
The total is $8 \times 15 = 120$. Taking out $22$ leaves $120 - 22 = 98$, shared among the $7$ numbers that remain. Divide to find the new mean.
Since $98 \div 7 = 14$, the mean of the remaining numbers is $14$.

learningObjective: Recompute a mean after removing a value.
explanation: The sum of the numbers is the mean times the count, so the original sum is $8 \times 15 = 120$.
Removing $22$ leaves a sum of $120 - 22 = 98$, and there are now $7$ numbers.
The new mean is $98 \div 7 = 14$. It is lower because the removed number was above the old mean.

alternativeExplanations.title: Predict the direction first
steps: Removing a value *above* the mean pulls the mean down; removing one below pushes it up.
Here $22 > 15$, so the new mean must be below $15$ — which rules out any choice at or above it.
Predicting the direction before computing turns a calculation into a check.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Dividing the new total by the OLD count — 98 ÷ 8 = 12.25 — is the engineered miss.
Removing a value changes both the sum and the count. Update the pair together: 98 across 7 values.
